question: Do continuously trained M1, M3-R, M4 replicate their development-set advantages over continuously trained IDM on the never-evaluated P1 sealed FourRoom split?
scope: One-time confirmatory evaluation of existing P7 checkpoints; no retraining, checkpoint selection, tuning, or test-driven iteration. M2 and B are secondary controls.

evaluation.success_event: first executed physical step t in 1..420 where native distance_to_target < 16
evaluation.task_payload_rule: Generate once from sealed split; SHA-freeze and reuse exact task payload for all 24 checkpoints; pair on episode index and reset seed. Do not inspect outcomes before all 24 jobs are complete.
evaluation.denominator: All 32 tasks for each checkpoint, including right-censored failures.

analysis.unit_of_training_variation: four training seeds; tasks are paired evaluation episodes, not 128 independent training runs
analysis.report: Every seed and arm, paired per-seed differences, median and range across seeds, per-task first-hit records; no best-seed selection or universal/significance claim from four seeds.
analysis.timing_claim: P7 early-versus-late analysis remains development-set evidence only; this P8 study does not test timing.
analysis.m2_claim: M2 outcome cannot be attributed solely to its mechanism without same-branch-data P7 control.
